concept.name: Sensitivity test
concept.definition: An analysis of how outputs change when specified inputs, parameters, or assumptions are varied over plausible values.
concept.intuition: It turns an informal trading idea into a claim or design choice that can be evaluated against dated evidence.
concept.mechanics: Select uncertain inputs and ranges before inspection, recompute results over the grid or scenarios, and report the response surface rather than only the best case.
concept.failure_modes: Results can mislead when hindsight, multiple testing, nonstationarity, costs, or unavailable historical information are ignored.
concept.misconceptions: A favorable historical result is evidence about the tested sample and assumptions, not proof of a durable profitable edge.
concept.example: Round-trip cost is varied from 5 to 50 basis points and net return turns negative above 28 basis points.
